title: Government’s Response to the “2026 Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament”
what_it_is: Government’s Response to the “2026 Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament”

sections.label: Public reaction to 9% salary increase
sections.summary: Some understood salary reviews but felt 9% was too high, comparing it with their own lower annual increments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Some could understand salaries being reviewed and adjusted, but felt that 9% was too high, instinctively comparing it with their own annual increments, which are considerably lower.

sections.label: Political salaries and benchmark update
sections.summary: Political salaries were not adjusted for 15 years since a 2011 downward restructuring, and the Committee recommends updating the MR4 benchmark from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Political salaries, by contrast, have not been adjusted for 15 years and importantly, that period begin not with an increase, but with a substantial downward restructuring in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Committee has now recommended that the MR4 reference benchmark be updated from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sections.label: Benchmark movement and income growth
sections.summary: The benchmark movement is about 3.6% a year over 15 years, while citizen incomes rose about 80% at median and 87% at P20 since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Spread over the 15 years since 2011, the movement in the benchmark works out to be about 3.6% a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Put it another way, since the 2012 review, incomes of Singapore Citizen earners have risen by about 80% at the median and 87% at P20.

sections.label: Benchmark versus paycheck and salary range
sections.summary: A benchmark is a reference point, not a paycheck, and Ministers can be paid within 75% to 125% of the reference salary for their grade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In wage-setting, a benchmark is not the same as your paycheck.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It is a reference point within a salary structure, and under the revised framework, Ministers can be paid within a range of 75% to 125% of the reference salary for their grade.

sections.label: Immediate 9% adjustment and future movements
sections.summary: The immediate adjustment is up to 9%, with no further special adjustments to close the gap, and later movements depend on performance and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The immediate adjustment is up to 9% and there will not be further special adjustments simply to close the gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Subsequent salary movements will depend on, rightfully, performance and responsibilities.

sections.label: Political pay linked to Singaporeans' outcomes
sections.summary: Part of political remuneration is linked to whether Singaporeans have jobs, real incomes grow, lives improve, and they realise their dreams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Part of the political remuneration is linked to how Singapore and Singaporeans are doing: whether people have jobs and whether their real incomes are growing, whether Singaporeans lives are improving, and that Singaporeans are able to realise their dreams and aspirations.

sections.label: Purpose of salary framework
sections.summary: The passage says scrutinising numbers should not obscure the framework's purpose of enabling capable people to serve and build a better tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: It is right that we scrutinise the numbers, the benchmarks and the wage framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We should not lose sight of why we have this framework in the first place – to enable capable people to step forward to serve, and together with every Singaporean to build a better tomorrow.

sections.label: No political salary increases
sections.summary: The Government did not increase political salaries in 2017 and 2023, and Minister and MP salaries have not been reviewed for about 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government chose not to increase political salaries in both 2017 and 2023, aware of the public sensitivities of doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It has been about 15 years since salaries for Ministers and Members of Parliament were reviewed.

sections.label: Committee's proposed salary increases
sections.summary: The Committee's report proposes raising the annual MP allowance package from $192,500 to $259,000 and an entry-level Minister's reference salary from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposals in the Committee's report, the annual MP allowance package will increase from $192,500 to $259,000, an increase explained largely by inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An entry-level Minister's annual reference salary, on the other hand, will increase from $1.1 million to $1.8 million dollars under the Committee's proposal.

sections.label: Prime Minister's proposed first-step increase
sections.summary: The Prime Minister proposed a first-step increase of up to 9%, said $1.8 million is not a target, and expects most MR4 Ministers at about $1.35 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In other words, the percentage increase for an MR4 Minister is roughly 1.8 times that of an MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That could explain why the Prime Minister has proposed a first-step increase of up to 9% and has committed that paying a Minister $1.8 million as laid out in the committee's report is not a target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister has also said that by the end of this term of Government, he expects most Ministers who remain at MR4 to be at the lower-end of the new salary range, at about $1.35 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At $1.1 million dollars today, the MR4 reference annual salary assumes 13 months of fixed pay and seven months of variable pay.

sections.label: Variable pay and bonus disclosure
sections.summary: The 2012 framework contemplated up to 13.5 months of bonus, and actual variable payments to Cabinet Ministers from 2013 to 2017 averaged 9.7 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we know that the 2012 framework for political salaries contemplated variable components, or a total bonus of up to 13.5 months a year, with the actual amount depending on the annual variable component, performance bonus and the National Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We also know that the Government disclosed that from 2013 to 2017, actual variable payments of the bonus to Cabinet Ministers averaged 9.7 months a year, not seven months as assumed by the annual salary norm in the Committee's report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Parliament in February this year, WP's Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Eileen Chong asked for the ranges of performance bonus, National Bonus and annual variable component received by Ministers from 2018 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: She did not receive a helpful reply from the Government, with only a range provided for the annual variable component at 0 to 1.5 months.

sections.label: WP candidates and Opposition seats
sections.summary: The passage says no WP candidate can assume victory or stand for parity in remuneration, and that at least one third of seats ought to be in Opposition hands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: No WP candidate can reasonably take for granted that he or she will win and become an MP, let alone approach the decision to stand for elections on the basis of achieving some degree of parity insofar as his or her renumeration prospects are concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We believe that our political system and our country is strengthened and not weakened by a strong and sensible Opposition in Parliament, where at least one third of the seats ought to be in Opposition hands.

sections.label: Mayor pay study recommendation
sections.summary: The committee recommended the Government study sizing payments for these roles de-linked from the MR4 benchmark, and the Government accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The committee has recommended that the Government study establishing a basis for sizing these payments for these roles that is de-linked from the MR4 benchmark while remaining adequate for these roles to be carried out faithfully and effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the recommendation and will undertake such a study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For clarity, the Minister for Public Services has confirmed that office holders receive one wage in addition to their MP's allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would follow that two out of five Mayors today receive a full Mayor's salary since the other three Mayors are office holders.

sections.label: Allowances last updated 2007
sections.summary: The Government confirmed these allowances were last updated in 2007, almost 20 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government also confirmed that these allowances were last updated in 2007 – almost 20 years ago.

sections.label: WP supports MP salary increase
sections.summary: The WP supports the increase in MP salaries in view of inflation and agrees with the Prime Minister not to increase Ministers' salaries beyond up to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To summarise, my clarifications notwithstanding, the WP supports the increase in salaries to MPs in view of inflation, and agrees with the decision of the Prime Minister not to increase the salaries of Ministers beyond up to 9%.

sections.label: National Bonus indicators
sections.summary: The National Bonus is determined by four indicators: citizen unemployment, real income growth at the median, real income growth at the 20th percentile and real GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, the National Bonus is determined by four economic and labour-market indicators: citizen unemployment, real income growth at the median, real income growth at the 20th percentile and real GDP growth.

sections.label: NCSS Quality of Life data
sections.summary: The NCSS has been measuring Quality of Life in Singapore for some years using internationally established instruments, giving national reference data.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The NCSS has been measuring Quality of Life in Singapore for some years, using internationally established instruments, and so, we now have national reference data.

sections.label: Essential Household Expenditure Basket
sections.summary: The passage asks whether an Essential Household Expenditure Basket could be considered for development.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could we therefore consider developing an Essential Household Expenditure Basket?

sections.label: Quality of Life measure framework
sections.summary: The speaker supports a robust Quality of Life measure including subjective indicators and suggests developing a broader social progress framework.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This brings me back to the Committee's proposal.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the inclusion of a robust Quality of Life measure, but not all indicators need to be objective.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A subjective measure allows Singaporeans themselves to tell us how they experience their lives.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am suggesting that as the Government develops its Quality of Life measure, we take the opportunity to develop a broader framework for understanding social progress.

sections.label: Quality of Life and National Bonus
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a broader social progress framework with objective and subjective measures will be considered, and notes the National Bonus recognises economy, jobs and incomes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And do Singaporeans themselves judge their quality of life to be good?

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, as Government considers and develops the proposed Quality of Life measure, will it consider a broader social progress framework incorporating objective as well as subjective measures?

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we can do this well, the National Bonus will continue to recognise the importance of a strong economy, jobs and rising incomes, whilst also recognising the reason these ultimately matter: to enable Singaporeans, their families and our communities to flourish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, in 2007, about a year after I entered Parliament, the Government moved a Motion to adjust the salaries of political appointment holders.

sections.label: Early long-term planning examples
sections.summary: Singapore had already begun planning the LNG terminal, Biopolis, Marina Bay and NEWater before energy security, biomedicine and water security became major concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: More than 20 years ago, before energy security became a major issue, we had already begun planning and building a liquefied natural gas terminal, giving Singapore more diversified sources of natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Before biomedicine became a major industry, the Government had already committed substantial resources to building Biopolis and nurturing a research, talent and industry ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To strengthen Singapore's position as an international financial centre and business hub, we began planning and developing Marina Bay decades ago, laying the foundations for the vibrant global city we see today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Before water security became a widely recognised global concern, Singapore had already begun developing NEWater.

sections.label: Salary framework and adjustment
sections.summary: The current framework uses market pay with a 40% discount, and the Prime Minister moderated the increase so serving Ministers initially receive a one-off adjustment capped at 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The current framework uses market pay as a reference point and applies a 40% discount to reflect the dedication and sacrifice inherent in public service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this round of adjustments, the Prime Minister has gone further by moderating the increase, such that serving Ministers will initially receive only a one-off salary adjustment capped at 9%.

sections.label: Energy expertise and PM Wong
sections.summary: The person understood energy markets and power generation, helped bring the LNG terminal to fruition, and Prime Minister Wong has led Singapore calmly since taking office in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: He had not only a deep understanding of how the energy market operated, but also a firm grasp of the technical issues underlying power generation and energy systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: He later played a direct role in bringing Singapore's liquefied natural gas terminal project to fruition, giving us multiple sources of natural gas and further strengthening our energy security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Since taking office in 2024, Prime Minister Wong has led Singapore with calmness and steadiness through an increasingly turbulent global environment.

sections.label: Political appointment holders' sacrifices
sections.summary: The speaker says political appointment holders' sacrifices exceed the 40% discount, errors in national strategy can be costly, and agrees it is time for an adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: If we compare the salaries of the Prime Minister and Ministers with those of corporate executives, and then consider the responsibilities and pressures borne by each, I believe many would agree that: the sacrifices made by political appointment holders in fact far exceed the 40% discount reflected in the current salary framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Particularly in major national strategies and public policies, an error of judgement or a wrong turn could carry an enormous cost and might even set the country on a path of non-return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For this very reason, when selecting and bringing in national leaders, we cannot compromise on the quality of leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I agree that it is time for an adjustment.

sections.label: Sustainable system for political leadership
sections.summary: The speaker says establishing a reasonable and sustainable system will encourage capable people of integrity to serve Singapore's political leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Twenty years on, I believe this is the right decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: If we want Singapore to continue to have an outstanding political leadership team in the decades ahead, we must establish a reasonable and sustainable system that encourages capable people of integrity and a strong sense of mission to step forward and serve the country.

sections.label: Scrutinising MR4 benchmark
sections.summary: The speaker asks what basis determines how much is enough and scrutinises the MR4 benchmark tying Ministerial salaries to top 1,000 earners' median income with a 40% discount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The question is: what is the appropriate, defensible and principled basis for determining "how much is enough"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to scrutinize the MR4 benchmark, which ties Ministerial salaries to the median income of the top 1,000 Singaporean earners, with a 40% discount.

sections.label: Comparable nations' leader remuneration
sections.summary: Heads of government in Switzerland, Luxembourg, Denmark, Germany and Belgium receive at most four to seven times their nation's median worker salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The heads of government in Switzerland, Luxembourg, Denmark, Germany and Belgium – nations with comparable standards of living and governance standards – receive remuneration that is, at most, four to seven times their nation's median worker salary.

sections.label: More gradual and modest path
sections.summary: The speaker says a more gradual and modest path, given the 9% phased increase already in motion, would have shown fiscal prudence and social sensitivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A more gradual and modest path, particularly given the 9% phased increase is already in motion, would have demonstrated fiscal prudence and social sensitivity.

sections.label: Fixed and variable salary split
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a fixed salary of 45% and variable component of 55%, weighted toward national performance metrics affecting the median citizen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we accept the premise of a clean wage, we must also accept the premise of shared risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose that we adjust the structure to a fixed salary of 45% and a variable component of 55%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The remaining 55% should be explicitly, transparently and heavily weighted toward national performance metrics that directly affect the median citizen – real median income growth, unemployment rates and housing affordability.

sections.label: Leadership past and present
sections.summary: The passage credits Mr Lee Kuan Yew's team, Mr Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong with Singapore's development and leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The late Mr Lee Kuan Yew, together with his pioneering team, transformed Singapore from a developing nation into a first world country within a single generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Goh Chok Tong and Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong, in their respective terms of leadership, continued to build on that foundation and helped raise the living standards of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has likewise demonstrated calm and purposeful leadership in guiding Singapore forward, with a clear commitment to ensuring that no Singaporean will be left behind.

sections.label: Ministerial pay and public service
sections.summary: Ministers should be paid fairly so pay is not a barrier, while rewards stay connected to the median Singaporean's well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My position is not that our Ministers should be paid poorly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They should be remunerated fairly and with dignity – they sacrificed a lot, their families sacrificed a lot – so that pay is never a barrier to capable and public-spirited Singaporeans entering public service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, let us ensure that the rewards of leadership remain meaningfully connected to the well-being of the median Singaporean.

sections.label: Revised benchmark figure
sections.summary: The revised benchmark is about 26 times the median gross income of around $69,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The revised benchmark is roughly 26 times the median gross income of around $69,000 a year.

sections.label: Government accepts review recommendations
sections.summary: The Government accepted the review committee's recommendations, reaffirmed the framework's core principles and updated the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the review committee's recommendations, reaffirmed the core principles of the framework and updated the benchmark.

sections.label: Prime Minister exercises pay restraint
sections.summary: The Prime Minister exercised restraint with a one-off adjustment of up to 9%, not an immediate leap to the new figure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: (In Malay): The Prime Minister has looked at that benchmark and exercised restraint: a one-off adjustment of up to 9%, not an immediate leap to the new figure.

sections.label: Donations, tax relief and salary ranges
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Prime Minister will claim tax relief on donations and says salary ranges should be widened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the Prime Minister claim tax relief on his donations?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In my view, the Prime Minister should not be financially worse off as a result of his decision to personally donate his salary increase to suitable charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is a second change that I think matters just as much: widening the salary ranges.

sections.label: Public service ethos discount
sections.summary: The framework recognises the ethos of public service through a 40% discount to the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The framework recognises the ethos of public service through a 40% discount to the benchmark, and I am glad it does.

sections.label: Decisions and salary adjustment
sections.summary: The speaker asks what made past answers no and whether money was unnecessary, and says the choice should not be made harder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Nobody writes a headline about the leader who never comes forward, but every time I hear that sentence, I ask myself what exactly made the answer no, and whether money was an unnecessary part of it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not know how many of those decisions a potential 9% adjustment would change, but I do know that we should not make the choice harder than it already is or needs to be.

sections.label: Performance-linked pay and National Bonus
sections.summary: 35% of remuneration is tied to performance, the National Bonus uses objective indicators with tightened targets, and the Prime Minister gains discretion over individual performance adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our system already ties part of remuneration – 35% – to performance, and I support that principle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The National Bonus is built on objective indicators, median income growth, income growth for our lowest earners, unemployment and gross domestic product (GDP), and I welcome that the targets behind them are being tightened further.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is perhaps somewhat less understood is the individual performance bonus and how individual performance of our political office holders is assessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is quite relevant, as under the revised arrangement, the Prime Minister will now also have the discretion to make subsequent salary adjustments tied to individual performance and responsibilities.

sections.label: Assessing Ministerial performance
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to confirm a robust performance assessment structure exists and to clarify the principles used to assess Ministerial performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that a robust structure exists to assess and recognise performance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide clarity on the principles used to assess Ministerial performance?

sections.label: Sacrifice, privilege and accountability
sections.summary: The speaker says sacrifice and privilege should be recognised and accountability demanded, and that updating the benchmark and widening the range do not weaken accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We should recognise the sacrifice because it is real and it falls not only on those who serve, but on the families who stand beside them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We should honour the privilege because very few people will ever be entrusted with it, and we should demand the amanah – the accountability, the standard, the humility that must come with it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Updating the benchmark does not lighten that demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And widening the range does not weaken accountability, it strengthens the principle that appointment is not the end of the test, it is the beginning of it.

sections.label: Political leadership Singapore needs
sections.summary: The speaker says questioning the number is fair, but the real question is what political leadership Singapore needs and whether the system attracts and judges capable Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Her instinct to question the number is fair and always will be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But the question is really about the kind of political leadership Singapore needs, and whether we have a system that can continue to attract capable Singaporeans, judge them fairly, recognise performance and hold them to the trust we place in them.

sections.label: MR4 benchmark and occupational breakdown
sections.summary: The MR4 benchmark uses the median income of the top 1,000 Singapore Citizen earners before a 40% discount, with 54.1% in senior management, 35.3% in financial services and 10.6% professionals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MR4 benchmark is based on the median income of the top 1,000 Singapore Citizen earners, before applying the 40% discount for political service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The occupational breakdown is quite concentrated: 54.1% are in senior management positions; another 35.3% are in financial services; and the remaining 10.6% are professionals, such as lawyers, accountants, doctors and engineers.

sections.label: Role-based comparator benchmark
sections.summary: Suggests future reviews test the top 1,000 benchmark against a role-based comparator built from what people in those roles earn.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, examine what people in those roles actually earn.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am not suggesting we abandon the current approach, but perhaps future reviews should test the top 1,000 benchmark against a role-based comparator constructed on this basis.

sections.label: Multi-year average earnings
sections.summary: Suggests examining three- or five-year average earnings instead of relying only on a single year's realised income.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And because Ministerial service typically unfolds over several years, we should also ask whether a one-year snapshot gives a representative picture of what people in that comparative group earn over a similar period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I suggest examining three- or five-year average earnings, rather than relying only on a single year's realised income.

sections.label: Width of talent pool
sections.summary: Raises the second question of how wide the talent pool should be kept open.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the second question, Sir, how wide the talent pool we should keep open.

sections.label: Questioning the 40% discount
sections.summary: Questions the 40% discount, saying an appropriate benchmark of comparable roles may not warrant a discount.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is a difference between someone willingly accepting sacrifice because of a sense of service and designing a compensation system that requires financial sacrifice as evidence of that service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And this leads me, Sir, to question the 40% discount, which the Committee's report describes as reflecting the ethos of political service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But if we first establish an appropriate benchmark based on genuinely comparable roles, I am not convinced that the logic warrants a discount to begin with.

sections.label: Compensating premium over discount
sections.summary: States the points support a compensating premium rather than an automatic discount.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my view, they support a compensating premium rather than an automatic discount.

sections.label: National stewardship scorecard
sections.summary: Suggests developing a long-term national stewardship scorecard alongside the National Bonus framework, assessing three-to-five-year progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, I suggest that the Government develop a long-term national stewardship scorecard alongside the National Bonus framework, assessing three-to-five-year progress towards long horizon outcomes and milestones.

sections.label: MP role and benchmark
sections.summary: It proposes starting with the MP role's responsibilities and then identifying a comparative group and standalone MP benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, as with Ministerial compensation, we should begin with the role itself, its responsibilities, its weight of decisions, the time commitment, constituency responsibilities, legislative work and public accountability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, identify an appropriate comparative group and develop a standalone MP benchmark.

sections.label: Comparator and earnings adjustments
sections.summary: It sets out identifying role-based comparators, examining earnings trajectory and persistence, and replacing the political service discount with an adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, identify roles that fairly reflect the skills, judgement and the weight of responsibility expected of our political office holders, and test the top 1000 benchmark against a role-based comparator.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, examine the trajectory and persistence of earnings rather than relying only on a one-year snapshot when establishing the compensation benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, once we have a credible comparator, replace the application of a political service discount with an adjustment that reflects the distinctive burden of political office.

sections.label: MP remuneration and sustainability
sections.summary: It proposes a standalone role-based framework for MP remuneration and a review of whether the MP role is sustainable long term.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fifth, develop a standalone role-based framework for MP remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And sixth, review whether the MP role itself is sustainable so that those who step forward can continue giving their best to Singaporeans over the long term.

sections.label: Private sector healthcare career
sections.summary: The speaker describes over three decades in the private sector as a doctor, healthcare entrepreneur, founder and head of a global private healthcare conglomerate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For more than three decades before entering politics, I was in the private sector, practising first as a doctor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I later became involved in the business of healthcare as an entrepreneur, a founder of a healthcare enterprise, and subsequently as the head of a global private healthcare conglomerate Medicine has a way of teaching you what truly matters.

sections.label: Gradual realisation to enter politics
sections.summary: The speaker says no single defining moment led him to leave his career, but a growing realisation he could give back to country and people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The truth is there was not a single defining moment that led me to leave my fulfilling career for the hurly-burly of politics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It was a gradual but a growing inner realisation that whatever experience I had accumulated over those years in the private sector could perhaps be put to good use in a different way, not just to change a few lives at a time or to build an organisation, but to give back to my country and my people.

sections.label: Ministerial salary versus prior earnings
sections.summary: The speaker says no realistic Ministerial salary could have matched what he earned before joining the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Speaking only for myself, no realistic level of Ministerial salary could have matched what I was earning before I joined the Government.

sections.label: Surgeons entering politics, salaries
sections.summary: The speaker cites surgeons like Dr Vivian Balakrishnan and Dr Ng Eng Hen whose ministerial salaries could not match what they gave up financially.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Imagine then, I had a lot of brilliant surgeons who were my colleagues in the private sector and in the public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But someone like my colleague, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, when he entered politics, or my former colleague, Dr Ng Eng Hen, their Ministerial salaries could never have matched what they gave up financially.

sections.label: Recruiting able people into politics
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore can keep people of ability, integrity and experience in political service if entry costs too much personally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The question is more fundamental: can Singapore continue to have people of ability, integrity and experience from every walk of life in political service?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If we make entry into the public service come at too high a personal cost for too many capable Singaporeans, then over time, we will indeed narrow the pool from which our country can draw its leaders from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And Members of the House, that would be a far greater cost than any salary we debate in this House.

sections.label: Government strength and recruitment
sections.summary: The passage states the strength of the Government depends on recruiting the best people to serve, not on what they are paid.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Because at the end of the day, the strength of our Government depends not on what we pay those who serve but on whether we can continue to recruit the best people to serve.

sections.label: Three principles of framework
sections.summary: The Minister named three principles the framework rests on: calibre, commitment, clean.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister named three principles the framework rests on: calibre, commitment, clean.

sections.label: Four national numbers and PM's view
sections.summary: The passage says part depends on four national numbers and part on the Prime Minister's view of each of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Part depends on four national numbers: how fast economy grows; how fast real incomes grow for the family, for the middle and for the lowest fifth; and how many citizens are out of work; part depends on the Prime Minister's view of each of them.

sections.label: Reporting aims and outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker asks that for each outcome the Government already reports, it state on one page what it aimed for, reached and did not.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My first ask is therefore for each outcome the Government already reports, say what it aimed for, what it reached and what it did not, on one page that anyone can read.

sections.label: Measuring Singaporeans living well
sections.summary: The speaker's second ask is to measure whether Singaporeans are living well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second ask is the one I care about most: measure whether Singaporeans are living well.

sections.label: Government exploring robust measure
sections.summary: The Government agreed to explore a robust one.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government agreed to explore a robust one.

sections.label: Ministerial clean wage compensation
sections.summary: Singapore compensates Ministers transparently through a clean wage, with no hidden allowances, so they are not incentivised to look elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Rather than expecting Ministers to rely on gifts, outside interest or other lucrative opportunities after leaving office, Singapore compensates them transparently through a clean wage, one that is sufficient to ensure that they are not incentivised to look elsewhere to make up the difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It means every Singaporean knows exactly how Ministers are remunerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are also no hidden allowances, no need to spend one's time in office preparing for the next career.

sections.label: Ministers' loyalty to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The model of Ministerial salaries seeks to guarantee that Ministers owe their loyalty, judgement and decisions to Singaporeans only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They must be able to do so without worrying about planning or pleasing benefactors, cultivating future employers or positioning themselves for life after politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is what our model of Ministerial salaries seeks to guarantee: that Ministers owe their loyalty, judgement and decisions to one group only ‒ Singaporeans.

sections.label: MP workload increased exponentially
sections.summary: The load has increased exponentially over the last 15 years for Government MPs, non-Government MPs, Non-Constituency MPs and Nominated MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Be it Government MPs, non-Government MPs, Non-Constituency MPs, Nominated MPs, one cannot disagree that the load has increased exponentially over the last 15 years.

sections.label: MP remuneration inflation increase
sections.summary: The speaker agrees that using inflation as the basis for increasing MPs' remuneration is in principle correct, and that the increase should not pay longer serving MPs more than first-term MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I agreed then, and I still agree today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, on the question of MPs just going on inflation as the basis for the increase in remuneration for Members of this House is, in principle, the correct thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I also agree that the increase should not be designed to compensate existing MPs for the exponential increase in the work by paying longer serving MPs more than first-term MPs.

sections.label: Political salary norms unchanged 15 years
sections.summary: Political salary norms have remained unchanged for 15 years, and the speaker agrees with Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's quote on capable Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Political salary norms have thereafter remained unchanged for 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A significant quote in Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's Statement in this House on Tuesday was this: "The idea that we can have less capable Ministers sitting above a first-rate civil service and everything will somehow continue to work, is a fantasy." I completely agree.

sections.label: Allowances and demands on office holders
sections.summary: Demands on office holders have increased, and the speaker hopes their allowances will be re-assessed, citing Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on political leadership quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While they were not mentioned in the report, it should be emphasised that demands on them have correspondingly increased, along with increased demands on every Member of this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I do hope their allowances will be re-assessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Tuesday, "It is ultimately about whether Singapore will continue to have the quality of political leadership we need to take our country forward." That, to me, is the essence and soul of this debate.

sections.label: No amount recompenses leaders
sections.summary: The speaker states that no amount could ever recompense leaders like Prof Jayakumar and Senior Minister Teo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Let us remember – no amount could ever recompense leaders, like Prof Jayakumar, Senior Minister Teo and so many others like them.

sections.label: Courage, conviction, principle over expediency
sections.summary: The report and two Statements show Singapore puts courage, conviction and principle ahead of political expediency, and the speaker supports the initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The report plus the two Statements on Tuesday display how in Singapore, courage, conviction and principle are put ahead of political expediency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am willing to put myself behind this initiative and I enjoin the whole House to support it.

sections.label: Flexible salaries for junior office holders
sections.summary: Junior political office holders' salary scales must be flexible, possibly with transitional arrangements like 60% of last drawn pay, with no stigma on returning to the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many of us would like to see more leaders and senior professionals from the private sector step forward to serve.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But for those new to political or public service, it would usually be appropriate for them to start in junior political appointments rather than lead a Ministry in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The salary scales of junior political office holders must therefore be sufficiently flexible to accommodate them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One possibility that could be considered as a transitional arrangement for those taking especially large pay cuts – for instance, giving them 60% of their last drawn pay, subject to an appropriate cap and limited to the first two or three years before their pay reverts to the normal benchmark for their substantive appointment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some may wish to serve for a limited period while others may find that political office is not a good fit after all.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should be no stigma attached to going back to the private sector after a term as an office holder.

sections.label: Lowering barriers to political entry
sections.summary: The overall aim is to lower barriers to entry for individuals and give Singapore a wider pool of potential political talent for future Cabinet Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The overall aim is to lower the barriers to entry for individuals while giving Singapore a wider pool of potential political talent, from which future Cabinet Ministers may be drawn.

sections.label: Objective of political pay
sections.summary: The objective is a wider and stronger pool of people willing and able to take on political leadership responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the objective is not high pay in itself, but a wider and stronger pool of people willing and able to take on the responsibilities of political leadership.

sections.label: MR4 reference salary rise
sections.summary: Under the unchanged formula, the MR4 reference salary rises from $1.1 million to $1.8 million, with the benchmark unchanged for 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Under the formula which has not changed, the MR4 reference salary rises from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Seen on it on its own, that is a substantial increase, but we should also understand why the gap has opened up, because the benchmark has effectively remained unchanged for 15 years, while salaries elsewhere in the economy have continued to move.

sections.label: Ministerial benchmark and civil servant pay
sections.summary: The Ministerial benchmark is lower than other top public positions, and civil servants joining politics see no pay increase, sometimes a cut.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The point is that different remuneration frameworks constructed for different senior public responsibilities have arrived at broadly comparable orders of magnitude and the Ministerial benchmark continues to be lower than what we pay for other positions carrying the highest levels of public responsibilities, because political service incorporates a more substantial discount.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is a perception that civil servants joining politics enjoy a pay increase.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is no increase when civil servants join politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Sometimes, it is even a pay cut, and when you look at the earnings over subsequent years for civil servants, if they had stayed on and done well, they would very likely have earned more in the Civil Service, as I have explained just now.

sections.label: Committee areas for study
sections.summary: The Government accepts the Committee's identified areas for study, including a quality-of-life indicator and different benchmarks for certain officeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Committee itself has identified areas for study, which we accept as a Government – like a quality-of-life indicator for the National Bonus and different benchmarks for the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Mayors and MPs.

sections.label: Government response to recommendations
sections.summary: The Government could have responded in several ways but already held back from the recommended adjustment in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There are several ways the Government could have responded to the Committee's recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we have already held back from making the recommended adjustment in 2017.

sections.label: Timing of salary adjustment
sections.summary: There is never a politically convenient time to adjust political salaries, and the review Committee was convened in December 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But there is never going to be a politically convenient time to adjust political salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We convened the review Committee in December 2025.

sections.label: Two support packages rolled out
sections.summary: Two support packages have been rolled out to help businesses, households and families.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Since then, we have rolled out two support packages to help businesses, households and families.

sections.label: Leadership renewal pressing and urgent
sections.summary: The need for leadership renewal is already pressing and urgent.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, as I have mentioned, the need for leadership renewal is already pressing and urgent.

sections.label: One-off salary adjustment of 9%
sections.summary: A one-off adjustment of up to 9% was decided, as the salary structure was frozen for 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But neither is it reasonable to leave their salaries unchanged indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why I decided on a one-off adjustment of up to 9%.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That takes into account the fact that the salary structure has been frozen for 15 years.

sections.label: PM donates salary increase
sections.summary: For the next five years, the Prime Minister will donate the full increase in his salary to good causes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Once the MR4 reference salary is updated, the Prime Minister's reference salary moves accordingly.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why for the next five years, I have decided to donate the full increase in my salary to good causes.

sections.label: Full adjustment cost $5 million
sections.summary: Minister Chan explained that a full one-off 9% adjustment for every office holder would cost $5 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Minister Chan explained in his speech that even if every office holder received the full one-off adjustment of 9%, the additional expenditure would be $5 million.

sections.label: Political office holder salaries cost
sections.summary: Salaries for all political office holders currently cost around $55 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, the salaries for all political office holders cost around $55 million.

sections.label: Assessing Ministers
sections.summary: The speaker says Ministers are not assessed based on one speech, controversy or headlines.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: When I assess Ministers, I do not do so based on one speech, one controversy or one set of headlines.

sections.label: Time and support for office holders
sections.summary: New office holders are given time and support to grow, but sustained underperformance may lead to a change.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: My approach has been to give new office holders time and support to grow into their roles and develop their strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But if there is sustained underperformance, at some point, I will have to make a change.

sections.label: Ministers held to highest standards
sections.summary: Ministers are held to the highest standards and must leave where those standards are breached.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ministers are held to the highest standards and where those standards are breached, they will have to leave.

sections.label: CDCs and Mayors value
sections.summary: The WP proposed abolishing the Mayor office, but the speaker cites CDC and Mayor contributions to communities and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: WP has proposed to abolish the office of Mayor.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But look at the value that the CDCs and Mayors have brought to our communities and to Singapore, mobilising a wider network of volunteers, responding to local needs and contributing to initiatives, like the CDC Vouchers and the Jobs Nearby scheme.

sections.label: Pay not incentive for politics
sections.summary: The speaker says PAP does not use higher pay as an incentive to draw people into politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is my key pre-requisite when I identify candidates to be fielded in any election.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to be very clear, for the PAP and the PAP Government, we do not believe in using higher pay as an incentive to draw people into politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, no one should enter politics for the money.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Competitive salaries do not create the motivation to serve.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But they can make it possible for someone who already has that motivation in the first place to step forward.

sections.label: Salary framework financial costs
sections.summary: The salary framework aims to avoid making financial costs unnecessarily high for those entering politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We should not require them to completely upend the financial responsibilities that they have legitimately taken up for their families.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, the purpose of the salary framework is to ensure that on top of all the other sacrifices involved, we do not make the financial costs unnecessarily high for them.

sections.label: Ministerial salary principles and differences
sections.summary: The parties agree on principles and moves this term, differing mainly on the formula and MR4 reference salary.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we agree on the key principles, as I have said earlier, that salaries must be competitive while incorporating a substantial discount for public service.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, we broadly agree on the moves to be made in this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where we differ is mainly on the formula, and therefore the appropriate MR4 reference salary for the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But in this term of Government, there is no practical difference because the Government is taking a gradual and restrained approach in implementation, moving ministerial MR4 salaries initially to $1.2 million and even by the end of this term to $1.35 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we were to update the MR4 benchmark by inflation, we will get a higher figure of $1.5 million.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Beyond that we will have to consider the circumstances then.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And five years from now there will be another independent review.

sections.label: Political salary framework goal
sections.summary: The political salary framework aims to give range and flexibility to choose and secure a strong, diverse team.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Likewise, the goal of the political salary framework is to give us the range and flexibility to choose and secure a strong and diverse team.

sections.label: MR4 benchmark not entitlement
sections.summary: The new MR4 benchmark is a reference point, not an entitlement, with capped adjustments and no near-term move to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As Members Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Yeo Wan Ling have noted, the new MR4 benchmark is a reference point and not an entitlement.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It is not the actual salary of every Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, for serving MR4 Ministers, there is no immediate move from $1.1 million to $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The one-off adjustment now is capped at up to 9%, differentiated by individual circumstances, including performance and when the person's salary was last adjusted.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: A Minister currently at $1.1 million will receive no more than about $1.2 million, with subsequent adjustments depending on performance and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, beyond the immediate adjustment this October, there is no intention to move all Ministers to $1.8 million in the near term.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has stated, we expect most MR4 Ministers to be at the lower end of the new salary range by the end of the term.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This means $1.35 million, and not $1.8 million.

sections.label: Fixed and variable salary split
sections.summary: About 65% of the annual salary is fixed and about 35% is variable.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Only about 65% of the annual salary is fixed, with about 35% being variable.

sections.label: National Bonus criteria and payouts
sections.summary: The National Bonus considers economic growth, jobs and real incomes, with payouts from 0.75 to 5.63 months since 2011.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The National Bonus not only looks at whether the economy grows, it looks at whether Singaporeans have jobs, it looks at whether real incomes are improving, after factoring in inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And since 2011, the National Bonus payout has ranged from 0.75 months in low years to 5.63 months in better years.

sections.label: Committee on two-third split
sections.summary: The Committee considered all this and felt the current two third, one third split is about right.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Committee has considered all this and on balance, they felt that the current two third, one third split is about right.

sections.label: Political salary spending limits
sections.summary: With the maximum 9% adjustment, political appointment holder salary spending is expected to stay below 0.05% of government expenditure and 0.01% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Assuming the maximum 9% adjustment, overall spending on political appointment holder salaries is expected to remain below 0.05% of government expenditure and below 0.01% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Even if with the new benchmark fully implemented, we will still spend less as a percentage of government expenditure and GDP than what we did in 2011.

sections.label: Top 1,000 benchmark purpose
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said the top 1,000 was never intended to identify jobs comparable to the Ministers.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister said, the top 1,000 was never intended to identify jobs comparable to the Ministers.

sections.label: Benchmark flexibility for archetypes
sections.summary: Regardless of formula or benchmark, the framework must let any Prime Minister have range and flexibility to bring in the three archetypes.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Then, the question is, how do we identify those roles and will we get back to the same situation when we first started, where we were looking at, perhaps leadership positions in companies, senior doctors, lawyers, and so forth, and then we had fewer vocations, fewer people.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, regardless of which formula and which benchmark we choose, we still need to ask one basic question: will this benchmark, will this framework allow the Prime Minister, any Prime Minister, to have the range and the flexibility to bring in that three archetypes that I talked about?

sections.label: MP and Mayor allowance benchmark
sections.summary: The government agrees to examine the benchmark for MP and Mayor allowances, since the MP allowance being a fraction of the MR4 benchmark is not intuitive.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: On the standalone framework for the MPs and the Mayors, we agree with the Committee's recommendation that we should examine the benchmark.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We agree that it is not so intuitive to say that the MP allowance – and it is not a pay, it is an allowance – is a fraction of the MR4 benchmark.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, we will study this and we will talk to various stakeholders to try and see what a better benchmark can be.

sections.label: Legislative and Secretarial Assistant allowances
sections.summary: No change was made to Legislative Assistant and Secretarial Assistant allowances because they were not under the political salaries terms of reference.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Members Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Christopher de Souza spoke on allowances for Legislative Assistants and Secretarial Assistants.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We did not make any change in this exercise because it was not under the terms of reference for the political salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But we will certainly look at how we can update this.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I will certainly task the relevant agencies to take a look at this, to update this as necessary.

sections.label: Salary range versus Committee recommendation
sections.summary: Depending on the assumed National Bonus, the range of numbers is about $1.5 million, compared to the Committee's recommended $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The range of the numbers, depending on what the Member assume to be the National Bonus, is about $1.5 million, compared to what the Committee has recommended, which is $1.8 million.

sections.label: Performance pay up to $1.35 million
sections.summary: After 15 October 2026, those whose performance deserves it may get up to $1.2 million, and by the end of the term up to $1.35 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: After 15 October 2026, those whose performance deserve it may get up to $1.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And if performance warrants it, responsibility warrants it, by the end of the term, those who have fulfilled the criteria may get up to $1.35 million.

sections.label: Variable component of Ministerial salary
sections.summary: Performance bonus ranged three to six months a year, averaging 4.3 months over five years, giving 9.7 months of variable component for Ministerial salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: For performance bonus, the range was from three to six months a year, with the average across all the political office holders over five years at 4.3 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, what one does is, you add 4.3, you add the National Bonus, you add the annual variable component, you get 9.7 months of the variable component for Ministerial salary.

sections.label: National Bonus in a good year
sections.summary: In a good year exceeding the target, the Minister may get more than the three months' norm as National Bonus, which back-tested would have tightened it by a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If there is a good year and we exceeded the target, the Minister will be able to get more than the three months' norm as a National Bonus, which is what I have shared with the Member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we have back-tested this, it would have tightened the National Bonus by a month.

sections.label: Continued debate and review committees
sections.summary: To Mr Saktiandi's questions, debate will continue with many opportunities to discuss further, and subsequent review committees will gather as much feedback as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To Mr Saktiandi's specific questions, yes, we will continue to debate this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There will be many opportunities to discuss further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And second, yes, we will continue through subsequent review committees to get as much feedback as possible.

sections.label: Systems against squandering wealth
sections.summary: Systems and processes exist to avoid squandering wealth, enshrined in the Constitution through Reserves principles, fiscal rules, incorruptibility and avoiding money politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the first point about systems and processes and institutions to ensure that we do not squander our wealth, we do have that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is enshrined in our Constitution through the Reserves principles, through our fiscal rules and more importantly, at the end of the day, through our entire system and our emphasis on incorruptibility and keeping our system clean and making sure that we never get into money politics.

sections.label: Variable bonus and $1.8 million
sections.summary: 13.5 months is the variable bonus; the Committee's proposal is based at seven months, and with the fixed component equals $1.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I will try again: 13.5 months is the variable bonus; the proposal from the Committee is based at seven months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, if the Minister says seven months is the variable, and including the fixed component, it is equal to $1.8 million.

sections.label: Ministerial salary payout information
sections.summary: Minister says he intends to provide more information on salary bands and variable payouts in broad ranges, but not individual grades or bonuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because as I understand it, he was asking about the fact that actual salary received by an office holder may differ from the norm because of the variable components, and there is data on the National Bonus, but not on the individual performance bonus in past years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not have the data with me in terms of what exactly the minimum-maximum was in those years, but what I have said in my speech, and I reiterate again, I do intend to look at how, given the interest in where the salary bands are, where Ministers lie in terms of the salary ranges and how the variable payouts will be, to see how we can provide more information to the public where these payouts are concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will not be able to tell you this individual is at what grade, what performance bonus, obviously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But giving such information in broad ranges, I think that is reasonable.

sections.label: Motion on Ministerial Statements lapses
sections.summary: Under Standing Order 44(2), the Motion to consider two Ministerial Statements on the 2026 salary review lapses at the conclusion of debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 44(2), the Motion to consider the two Ministerial Statements delivered on 8 September 2026, on the Government's response to the "2026 Review of Salaries for Political Appointment Holders and Members of Parliament" lapses at the conclusion of debate.
